title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 346 (Inspection of books and papers by creditors and contributories)

content.overview: At any time after the making of an order for the winding up of a company by the Tribunal, any creditor or contributory of the company may inspect the books and papers of the company only in accordance with, and subject to such rules as may be prescribed. Nothing in the section excludes or restricts rights conferred by any law on the Central or State Government, any authority or officer thereof, or any person acting under their authority.
content.glance: After Tribunal winding-up order, creditors and contributories may inspect books/papers subject to prescribed rules; Government inspection rights preserved.
content.study: Section 346 regulates post-order inspection. Once a Tribunal winding-up order is made, any creditor or contributory may inspect the company’s books and papers only in accordance with and subject to such rules as may be prescribed. The section does not exclude or restrict inspection or other rights conferred by any law on the Central Government, a State Government, any authority or officer thereof, or any person acting under their authority.

examples.title: Creditor inspection
examples.body: A creditor seeks to inspect the company’s ledgers after the winding-up order. Access is available only in accordance with the rules prescribed under s. 346.

hypotheticals.question: Does s. 346 apply to voluntary winding up?
hypotheticals.analysis: The inspection right under sub-section (1) is triggered by a Tribunal winding-up order; it does not by its terms apply to voluntary winding up.
